newsitem.title: USA: Fox Television to merge its children's network.
newsitem.headline: Fox Television to merge its children's network.

text.p: Fox Broadcasting Co. said on Monday it is merging its Children's Network with Saban Entertainment, which produces "Mighty Morphin Power Rangers" and has an extensive library of programming for kids.
Under the agreement, the two companies will form a new holding company with Saban Chairman Haim Saban overseeing all Saban-related production and distribution.
Margaret Loesch, chairman of the Fox Kids Network, will handle that company's operations. Fox Broadcasting is owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp. of Australia.
Terms of the transaction were not disclosed, but a Fox spokesman said that it did not involve the exchange of any cash.
The Fox Children's Network produces such shows as "Goosebumps", "Casper the Friendly Ghost", "Spiderman" and "The Adventures of Batman and Robin".

Fox has been affiliated with the privately-held Saban since last October, when they formed an alliance to launch children's television channels around the world. They have since then cemented plans to launch satellite and cable children's services in Britain and in Latin America.
"By forming this new company, we now have the strength and resources necessary to build a truly worldwide children's entertainment business," Loesch said in a statement.

Sources close to the deal said the merger should help both companies expand globally and better compete with other giants in children's programming such as Time Warner Inc and ABC owner Walt Disney Co.
He also declined to comment on published reports that the new entity would seek to raise money through a stock or debt offering, but said, "we're considering many options."
Fox stressed that after the spin-off its stations will continue to carry Fox' so-called kidvid programming.
